solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Like this clue, a pain?

parts.note: a cross to bear is a burden or affliction

explanation.surface: A solver grumbles that this clue is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at the clue itself: this clue sits in the across column, so it is an ACROSS clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue is numbered among the horizontal entries, so its direction in the grid describes it.

clue.text: Recognition of program the French employ

parts.note: an app is a computer program
to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: Software is praised for the way French people use it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French' is a crossword staple for LA or LE; here the feminine form is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapping is public acknowledgement of a performance, so it serves as a form of praise or credit.

clue.text: Check features train tracks in part

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is wanted, so the letters lie inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: An inspection covers some of a railway's lines.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is featuRES TRAIN Tracks; 'features' reads like a verb in the surface but simply supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A check on something is a curb or limit, which is exactly what self-control or a restriction provides.

clue.text: Queen is looking up colour

indicators.note: in a down entry, looking upward means the letters read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A queen glances upward at a shade of paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' usually suggests ER or R, but here a named queen is needed, and only ANNE fits with IS when flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earthy brownish pigment, an example of a paint shade.

clue.text: One presents expert with difficult question

parts.note: a pro is a professional or expert
a poser is a puzzling problem

explanation.surface: A quizmaster confronts a specialist with a tough question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One presents' looks like the start of a sentence about a host, but it is the definition: someone who puts forward a motion.
explanation.definitionFit: In a debate the person who formally puts forward a motion is called by this title.

clue.text: Logical, with particular focus on country, after change at top

indicators.note: a change at the top means the opening letter is swapped for another one

parts.note: putting special emphasis on one's own nation

explanation.surface: Sensible thinking about a country follows a change of leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first letter N of NATIONALISTIC for R; the clue leaves the new letter for the solver to find.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning-based thought relies on reason and argument, so it is a synonym for being sound in reasoning.

clue.text: Sign left on part of hospital

indicators.note: in a down entry, one thing placed on another sits above it, fixing their order

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A notice is left on a hospital ward door.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT (ear, nose and throat) is the standard crossword hospital department.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen or warning of what is to come is a type of sign, especially a foreboding one.

clue.text: Room superb after singular pressure

indicators.note: one thing coming after another puts it second in the line

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A great room comes after a single source of stress.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the excellent part first but places it last in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Having room means having available area or capacity, the same uncountable sense.

clue.text: Give account of riotous excesses, initially after hours

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words before it

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words
after hours means late at night

explanation.surface: Someone describes their wild behaviour late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After hours' reads as a time phrase linking the parts, but it is a block in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate or tell a story is to describe events in words, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Penny, sob sister, regularly seen in group

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for penny

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Penny, a sentimental journalist, is often spotted in a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: A sob sister is a journalist who writes sentimental stories; here the phrase is only a letter source.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a band of people, originally summoned by a sheriff, now any gang or set of friends.

clue.text: Aware cult could somehow make you shriek!

indicators.note: somehow suggests an unspecified way of reworking, so the letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: A worldly-wise sect might somehow make a person scream.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark dresses up the definition; only the two opening words are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To yowl like a cat is to make a loud, harsh, wailing cry, which matches screaming.

clue.text: Kindly, arrive carrying type of fruit, date essentially

indicators.note: something carrying another holds it inside
the essence of a word is its core, so only the central letters stay

explanation.surface: A kind visitor brings fruit, perhaps dates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Date' looks like another fruit alongside the first, but only its central letters are used; the arriving word wraps around both the fruit and those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindly as an adjective means showing warm sympathy and concern for others' suffering.

clue.text: On way back, parent welcoming friend in Nato?

indicators.note: to welcome is to take someone in, so one part goes inside the other
travelling back means going in the opposite direction, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a crony is a close companion

explanation.surface: A mother returning home greets a pal serving in the military alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: Nato is formed from initials and pronounced as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization's short name is built from initial letters and spoken as a word, the textbook instance.

clue.text: Plain unlimited meal must be included for pig?

indicators.note: without limits means the boundary letters at each end are dropped
to be included is to be placed inside something else

parts.note: the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A pig needs a basic all-you-can-eat meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlimited' seems to go with 'Plain' but trims 'meal'. 'Pig' is a verb here, as in 'pig out'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pig is informal for gorging greedily, consuming far more food than needed.

clue.text: Small set of tools — source of mirth?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a kit is a set of tools or equipment

explanation.surface: A tiny toolkit is wondered at as a cause of amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the usual clothing-size abbreviation for small.
explanation.definitionFit: A short comic sketch is performed to make an audience laugh.

clue.text: Rocky — a cab? List changes required

indicators.note: changes means alterations, so the order of these letters is altered

explanation.surface: Rocky, a taxi driver, is told the list needs revising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' looks like a boxer's name addressing the cab; it is an adjective meaning made of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Basalt is a dark volcanic stone, so the adjective describes something composed of that rock.

clue.text: Unexpectedly cool chat, ultimately memorable, sweet

indicators.note: something unexpected does not follow the predicted order, so the letters are scrambled
ultimately means in the end, so the final letter is kept

explanation.surface: A surprisingly relaxed conversation proves memorable and charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like an adjective praising the chat, but it is the noun: a confection.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet in British usage is a piece of confectionery, and this cocoa treat is a classic example.

clue.text: Shifted tardily about love? Too much of it?

indicators.note: to be about something is to go around it, enclosing it
shifted means moved about, so these letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone moved slowly around their beloved — perhaps loving too much?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue: 'it' is the love just mentioned, and an excess of it is worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship of an idol, or extreme devotion to a person, is adoration carried beyond reasonable bounds.

clue.text: Hard to believe at first some fashionable people sail in this

indicators.note: at first means at the start, so the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Amazingly, some trendy people go sailing in this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashionable people' looks like one phrase, but 'people' begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional square-rigged sailing vessel with high masts carries crews and trainees at sea.

clue.text: Looks, not nice, about a daily's opening opinion pieces

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Unpleasant appearances feature in a newspaper's first editorials.
explanation.walkthrough: In British newspapers a leader is the editorial column stating the paper's view.
explanation.definitionFit: Leading articles are the newspaper editorials expressing the publication's own view, hence comment columns.

clue.text: Suitable for purpose — well-behaved

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fit and adequate for the job
second meaning: obedient, as of a child

explanation.walkthrough: Two separate senses of one everyday word sit either side of the dash.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both adequate or serviceable for a task and obedient or virtuous in conduct.

clue.text: A politician visiting copper's place of learning

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone's home, so one part enters the other

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, plus S for the possessive

explanation.surface: A politician calls at a policeman's house of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer, but it is the metal, symbol Cu, and the 's of the possessive supplies S.
explanation.definitionFit: A university's grounds and buildings form the site where students study.

clue.text: Bring up subject of jewellery, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is speech, so the word is identified by its pronunciation

parts.note: a brooch is a pinned ornament, an item of jewellery

explanation.surface: Someone raises the topic of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring up subject' looks like the definition; but 'subject' belongs with 'of jewellery', meaning an item of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a topic for discussion is to introduce it, the usual verb with 'a subject'.

clue.text: Active at the start, outspoken almost to the end, party — Green?

indicators.note: going almost to the end means stopping one letter short
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: vocal means outspoken; its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: An activist, loud until the end, joins the Green Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party — Green' suggests politics; but the party is a social do and Green is a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Avocado is a shade of dull yellowish green named after the fruit's skin and flesh.

clue.text: Originally one very often in development, like some farm produce?

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so each word gives its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Something unique is often still being developed, like farm crops.
explanation.walkthrough: The farm produce is eggs, and the question mark flags this sideways definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid means egg-shaped, so it describes eggs collected from hens on a farm.

clue.text: Expression heard to fuel uproar

indicators.note: something heard is taken in through speech, so pronunciation counts

parts.note: a term is a word or expression

explanation.surface: A remark is overheard that stokes public outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, the two words run into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of great confusion and disorder is a commotion or tumult.

clue.text: Topic male developed referring to Sky viewer?

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new form, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A men's topic is worked up, about someone watching Sky television.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky looks like the British satellite TV company; it is the heavens, studied by the ancient astronomer Ptolemy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptolemy was the ancient Greek astronomer who mapped the heavens, so the adjective pertains to that stargazer.

clue.text: Expect a heavy load, by the sound of it

indicators.note: judging by sound means the spoken form is what counts

explanation.surface: Someone braces for a hefty delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, the two words merge into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To wait for something anticipated is to look forward to its arrival.

clue.text: Avoid team's darling, after reflection

parts.note: a side is a team, with S for the possessive

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the letters appear backwards

parts.note: pet is a term of endearment

explanation.surface: Having thought it over, someone shuns the squad's favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After reflection' sounds like careful thought, but it flips the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge an issue or person is to evade it, a figurative extension of stepping aside.

clue.text: Sound of surprise after church finally very forward

indicators.note: coming after something places it later in the line

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
eek is a cry of alarm

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A startled cry goes up in church; how bold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very forward' reads as one phrase, but 'very' gives its last letter and 'forward' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward as an adjective means presumptuous or impudent, matching an impertinent manner.
